verdict.rationale: GitCafe's own docs say a new account receives the SSH and GPG keys from the user's GitHub profile, so the forge stores GPG keys on accounts. Storing GPG keys only makes sense for checking commit signatures, but the evidence never says GitCafe verifies signed commits or shows a verified badge. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of commit signature verification, a verified indicator in commit views, SSH-signing support, a way to add signing keys directly, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can sign commits with GPG or SSH keys and have them shown as verified

citations.quote: Your new account also gets the SSH and GPG keys on your GitHub profile, with the default SSH access; keys GitCafe cannot use are skipped.
